description_full: Provident Financial Services, Inc. operates as the bank holding company for Provident Bank that provides various banking products and services to individuals, families, and businesses in the United States. Its deposit products include savings, checking, interest-bearing checking, money market deposit, and certificate of deposit accounts, as well as IRA products. The company's loan portfolio comprises commercial real estate loans that are secured by properties, such as multi-family apartment buildings, retail and industrial properties, and office buildings; commercial business loans; fixed-rate and adjustable-rate mortgage loans collateralized by one- to four-family residential real estate properties; residential mortgage loans; commercial construction loans; and consumer loans consisting of home equity loans, home equity lines of credit, personal loans and unsecured lines of credit, and auto and recreational vehicle loans. It also offers cash management, remote deposit capture, payroll origination, escrow account management, and online and mobile banking services; and business credit cards. In addition, the company provides wealth management services comprising investment management, trust and estate administration, financial planning, and tax compliance and planning; and insurance agency operations. Further, it sells insurance and investment products, including annuities; and manages and sells real estate properties acquired through foreclosure. The company was founded in 1839 and is headquartered in Jersey City, New Jersey.

financial_summary: Provident Financial Services, I is a mid-cap financial services business with a $3.0B market cap on $870M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +20% over the past three years and +11% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 12% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.

The business throws off $431M in free cash flow — roughly 49 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.52× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 4.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 2.8% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 1.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 47% operating margin runs 18pp above the Financial Services median (29%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.

mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 27% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 6% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 10% below the high.

On multiples it looks cheap against Financial Services peers: P/E 9.6 vs 12.2 and P/FCF 7.0 vs 12.9 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 49% below its 10-year median.
The 6 covering analysts target $27.83 on average, 21% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 9.1% annual cash-flow growth, 15pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 12% earns above the cost of capital of 8.8%, but the 3pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have been steady (CV 0.29).
It converts 49% of revenue into free cash flow.
It earns a 10% return on equity.

growth: Revenue has compounded at 19.9% over 3 years, 17.7% over 5 years and 11.1% over 10 years, so growth is accelerating.

own: Insiders own a modest 2.8%, and institutions hold 77%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (6 sales, net $2.0M sold).
It returns 4.2% a year to shareholders (4.2% in dividends).
The share count has grown 11.1% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
It has paid a dividend for 22 consecutive years, raising it 13.9% a year over the last five.
people: With about 1,817 employees, each generates about $479K of revenue, in line with the Financial Services median, and productivity has risen 9.0% a year.
